subject: Meteorology
title: Weather Radar History
description: A 60-second lesson on Weather Radar History.

hook.text: Weather radar was discovered by accident—WWII radar operators noticed precipitation was cluttering their displays.

buildup.text: What was noise for military radar became signal for meteorologists—rain and snow reflected the microwave pulses clearly.

discovery.text: By the 1950s, weather radar networks were tracking storms—showing precipitation intensity and movement in real time.

twist.text: Doppler radar, deployed in the 1990s, added wind data—revealing rotation inside storms before tornadoes form.

climax.text: Dual-polarization radar, added in the 2010s, distinguishes rain, hail, and snow—even detecting debris from tornadoes.

punchline.text: Military clutter became meteorology's most powerful ground tool.

quiz.question: How was weather radar originally discovered?
options: WWII radar operators noticed precipitation on their screens
